intro.text: NW Holdings is a holding company headquartered in Portland, Oregon and owns NW Natural, SiEnergy Operating, LLC (SiEnergy Gas Utility or SiEnergy), NW Natural Water Company, LLC (NWN Water Utility or NWN Water), and NW Natural Renewables Holdings, LLC (NWN Renewables). NW Natural distributes natural gas to residential, commercial, and industrial customers in Oregon and southwest Washington. NW Natural and its predecessors have supplied gas service to the public since 1859, was incorporated in Oregon in 1910, and began doing business as NW Natural in 1997. Prior to the first quarter of 2025, NW Natural's natural gas distribution activities were reported in the natural gas distribution (NGD) segment.

In addition, NWN Water provides water services to communities throughout the Pacific Northwest and California.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The NWN Gas Utility business serves residential, commercial, and industrial customers with no individual customer accounting for more than 10% of NW Natural's or NW Holdings' revenues.
No individual customer accounts for more than 10% of SiEnergy’s revenues.
During 2025, utility services accounted for 87% of NWN Water's operating revenues.

Public Utility Commission regulated utilities accounted for 64% of operating revenues, and an additional 23% of operating revenues come from water and wastewater utility services where NWN Water is the sole provider.
No individual customer accounts for more than 10% of NWN Water's revenue.

Single-family new construction has consistently been our largest source of growth.
The NWN Gas Utility business relies on segmentation of firm pipeline transportation capacity that flows from Stanfield, Oregon to various points south of Molalla, Oregon.

The cost of gas sold to NWN Gas Utility customers primarily consists of the following items, which are included in annual Purchased Gas Adjustment (PGA) rates: gas purchases from suppliers; charges from pipeline companies to transport gas to our distribution system; gas storage costs; gas reserves costs; gas commodity derivative contracts; and renewable natural gas and its attributes, including renewable thermal certificates.

To that end, NW Natural developed and implemented an emissions screening tool that uses Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) data to calculate the relative emissions intensity of gas producer operations and prioritize purchases from lower emitting producers.
Single-family new construction has consistently been SiEnergy's largest source of growth.

In order to implement our business strategy and serve our customers, we depend upon our continuing ability to attract and retain talented professionals and a technically skilled workforce, and being able to transfer the knowledge and expertise of our workforce to new and increasingly diverse employees as our older workforce retires.
